subject: Critical Thinking
title: Cross-Examination: The Art of Strategic Questioning
description: Learn Cross-Examination: The Art of Strategic Questioning in one minute.

hook.text: A lawyer asks: 'You said you were home all evening?' 'Yes.' 'Then why does this receipt place you at a gas station at.

buildup.text: Cross-examination: a structured period where one side questions the other, aiming to expose weaknesses.

discovery.text: The golden rule: never ask a question you don't know the answer to.

twist.text: Leading questions are the tool: 'Isn't it true that...?' forces yes/no answers that build a narrative the examiner.

climax.text: Defense: answer only what's asked, never volunteer, and don't guess. The examiner's power comes from your extra words.

punchline.text: In cross-examination, the questions are the argument.

quiz.question: What is the 'golden rule' of cross-examination?
options: Never ask a question you don't already know the answer to
Ask as many questions as possible

details.summary: Cross-examination uses targeted questions to test a claim's consistency and expose weaknesses. Great cross-examiners never ask a question they do not already know the answer to.
details.whyItMatters: Strategic questioning is indispensable in law, journalism, and any setting where you need to verify claims under pressure.
takeaways: Good cross-examination follows a planned sequence
Leading questions control the direction of testimony
The goal is to reveal inconsistency, not to argue

faq.question: What is the golden rule of cross-examination?
faq.answer: Never ask a question unless you already know the answer. Open-ended questions give the witness room to explain away inconsistencies. Closed questions control the narrative and trap contradictions.

faq.question: How can cross-examination techniques help outside the courtroom?
faq.answer: They help in job interviews, investigative journalism, and any negotiation where verifying claims matters. The core skill of testing consistency through sequence applies everywhere.
